citations.B1: Read-then-write on `counts` is not atomic, so two threads can both pass the check and exceed the limit
citations.B3: hold a lock (or use `dict.setdefault` plus an atomic counter) around the whole check-and-increment
citations.B4: Because there is no window, `limit` is a lifetime cap, not a rate
citations.B5: `counts` grows without bound as new user IDs arrive, leaking memory until the process dies
citations.B6: The counter is per-process in-memory state, so N workers each allow the full limit
citations.B7: `user_id` is trusted and unvalidated, so a `None` or unhashable value raises
